summary: Texas Forest Service tower near Mount Enterprise in Rusk County, erected by June 1936 at 100 ft and listed standing; 1950 patrolman; access not found.

staffing.status: R. S. Flanagan planned as patrolman in 1936; Rob Flannagan stationed at the tower in May 1950; no later staffing reported

events.note: June 1936 item says the Texas Forestry Service had erected the tower, 100 feet high, slightly north of Mount Enterprise
June 1936 item says the station would be manned by R. S. Flanagan and Terrell Collier; no later source confirms that crew
May 1950 item: crewleader Rob Flannagan stationed at the Mt. Enterprise lookout tower

evidence.supports: tower erected by the Texas Forestry Service, slightly north of Mount Enterprise in Rusk County
evidence.quote: A new watch tower has been erected in East Texas by the Texas Forestry Service.

evidence.supports: tower location slightly north of Mount Enterprise
evidence.quote: The latest tower is located slightly north of Mount Enterprise, in Rusk county.
The tower is 100 feet high, its chief purpose is to maintain a lookout for the prevention of forest fires.

evidence.supports: one of 19 watch towers being erected across the state
evidence.quote: This tower is one of the 19 watch towers which are now being erected over the state.

evidence.supports: towers to have telephones connecting each to its neighboring lookout
evidence.quote: The towers will also have telephone which will connect each tower with its neighboring lookout.

evidence.supports: station planned to be manned by R. S. Flanagan and Terrell Collier
evidence.quote: The station will be manned by R. S. Flanagan, patrolman, and Terrell Collier, assistant.

evidence.supports: May 1950: Rob Flannagan stationed at the Mt. Enterprise lookout tower
evidence.quote: Flannagan is stationed at the Mt. Enterprise lookout tower.

evidence.supports: May 1950: Jeep made possible by a fire-fighting cooperative near Mt. Enterprise
evidence.quote: Purchase of the Jeep was made possible largely through the formation of a forest fire fighting cooperative in the vicinity of Mt. Enterprise.

evidence.supports: co-op formed through efforts of B. W. Jackson and crewleader Flannagan
evidence.quote: The coop owes its formation to the unceasing efforts of B. W. Jackson, agriculture teacher at Mt. Enterprise, and crewleader Flannagan.

evidence.supports: Texas list shows the Mount Enterprise tower in Rusk County as standing

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The June 1936 item spells the patrolman R. S. Flanagan; the May 1950 item spells him Rob Flannagan. The sources do not say whether they name the same man, so the story says so.

notes_for_editor: The 1936 date comes from a June 1936 newspaper item saying the tower had been erected; no later construction record was read. The 1936 item calls the agency the Texas Forestry Service, a branch of A. and M. College; the Forest Lookouts page and the FFLA list use Texas Forest Service. Standing rests on the FFLA list only. A texasescapes.com article says some East Texas towers can still be found near Mount Enterprise; it is undated and general, so it is not used. No access source found. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 3 page reads plus the shared FFLA and Texas index pages.
